questions.idea: How much can models scheme without in-context goals / learning
questions.quote: The extent to which models can scheme without in-context learning remains an open question not addressed by this study.

questions.idea: Build propensity model organisms with intrinsic agentic motivations and hidden goals
questions.quote: To address these limitations and expand the scope of our scheming propensity evaluations, we identify several key directions for future research: Build model organisms for propensity evaluations that have intrinsic agentic motivations and hidden goals.

questions.idea: Explain the unprompted deceptive tendencies observed
questions.quote: We encourage further research to properly explain these phenomena.

questions.idea: Whether unsolicited deception scales with reasoning capability across realistic contexts
questions.quote: It remains to be seen whether LLMs exhibit patterns of unsolicited deception, whether they do so more in situations where deception might benefit a rational self-interested agent, and whether this context sensitivity scales with the apparent reasoning capability.

questions.idea: Whether CoT-monitoring evasion trends persist as capability increases
questions.quote: However, it remains an open question whether these trends will persist as models capabilities continue to increase.

questions.idea: Re-assess monitorability conclusions as models grow more capable
questions.quote: Future work will need to re-assess this conclusion as models grow more capable and are applied to new tasks.

questions.idea: Hybrid monitoring combining CoT with behavioral and internal signals under adversarial conditions
questions.quote: Future research should explore hybrid monitoring systems that combine CoT analysis with behavioral and internal model signals to maintain effectiveness even under adversarial conditions.

questions.idea: Compare RL-evaluation optimization pressure to training pressure as a driver of encoded reasoning
questions.quote: Section 3.7 explores potential drivers of encoded reasoning, though rigorously comparing the optimization pressure from RL evaluations to that experienced during training remains an open problem.

questions.idea: Investigate complex backdoor trigger conditions and scale/CoT-driven robustness of persistence
questions.quote: We leave investigation into complex backdoor trigger conditions for future work; robustness increases with model scale and with chain of thought.

questions.idea: Build a sandbagger that survives anti-refusal training
questions.quote: The next step is to attempt to build a sandbagger - a model modified to reduce its performance specifically on dangerous capability evaluations - that survives anti-refusal training.

questions.idea: Whether distribution shift lets advanced models sandbag scheming evaluations
questions.quote: Whether this distribution shift could lead to advanced models being able to sandbag such evaluations is an open question.

questions.idea: Improve Poser with more numerous, capable, diverse alignment-faking models
questions.quote: Future work could improve on Poser with more numerous, capable, and more diverse models that are more analogous to real alignment faking AI systems.

questions.idea: Study whether future AIs develop strong unintended preferences conflicting with training
questions.quote: Our results are least informative regarding whether future AIs will develop strong and unintended preferences that conflict with the training objective, suggesting these are important for future work.

questions.idea: Test cross-format transfer of the deception conflict signature and training-time evasion
questions.quote: We leave this cross-format transfer test to future work; whether a model trained to minimize its conflict signature can evade RIFT is the important open question.

questions.idea: Improve probe training sets, SHIFT-controlled generalization, and aggregation
questions.quote: Future work could explore if improved training sets, controlling generalization with SHIFT, or different aggregation techniques improve performance.

questions.idea: Principled joint selection of intervention layer and strength that generalizes across models
questions.quote: Developing more principled strategies for jointly selecting the intervention layer and strength - ones that account for distributional shift and generalize reliably across models and training sources - remains an important direction for future work.

questions.idea: Mechanistic interpretability to localize and target deception for detection and mitigation
questions.quote: Future work should systematically investigate how contextual framing modulates deception and employ mechanistic interpretability to identify specific architectural elements responsible, enabling more targeted detection and mitigation.

questions.idea: Establish appropriate evidence levels and research directions for scheming safety-case assumptions
questions.quote: We hope to start a discussion on appropriate evidence levels for each assumption, research directions to provide this evidence, and how safety case makers can address scheming.

questions.idea: Whether faster, iterated external safety-case review cycles are feasible and how many dialectic cycles are needed
questions.quote: Whether such a quicker review cycle is possible, how many dialectic cycles would be required and what this means for the review team could be a subject for future work.

questions.idea: Monitoring effectiveness in realistic coding environments with multi-step distributed sabotage
questions.quote: Future work should investigate monitoring effectiveness in more realistic coding environments where multi-step, distributed sabotage is possible.

questions.idea: Better elicitation of sabotage agents and monitors
questions.quote: Our elicitation methods are far from exhaustive, and we hope that future work will better elicit sabotage agents and monitors.

questions.idea: Address sandbagging as a key limitation of deceptive-capability elicitation
questions.quote: Sandbagging (intentional underperformance by the model) is an important challenge for evaluations of deceptive capabilities such as ours, and is a key limitation for future work to address.

questions.idea: Whether reinforcing undetectable vs overt reward hacks has different effects on alignment
questions.quote: It is possible that reinforcing only undetectable reward hacks rather than overt reward hacks has different effects on alignment, but we leave this distinction for future work.

questions.idea: Harden control protocols with stronger red-teaming, monitor ensembling, robust data-routing
questions.quote: These findings highlight the need for future work on control protocols to incorporate stronger red-teaming and worst-case analysis and to mitigate monitor vulnerabilities, either by monitor ensembling or by adopting robust data-routing mechanisms.

questions.idea: Lower-bound the number of subtle collusion strategies under poorly understood training dynamics
questions.quote: How to lower-bound n_s remains an important open question since it depends on poorly understood training dynamics.

questions.idea: Collusion detection that adapts to varying agent counts and colluder/honest splits
questions.quote: Future work could develop methods that adapt to varying N and to arbitrary splits between colluding and honest agents, including the case where colluders outnumber honest ones.

questions.idea: How contextual framing modulates deception
questions.quote: Future work should systematically investigate how contextual framing modulates deception.

questions.idea: Characterize the statistical properties of the sandbagging likelihood-ratio test
questions.quote: Further research might aim to mathematically characterise the statistical properties of the likelihood ratio test as a function of the horizon parameters.

questions.idea: Whether prompt techniques (deontological framing, scratchpad) robustly prevent alignment faking across small LLMs
questions.quote: Further research may explore the impact of prompting techniques like deontological framing and scratchpad reasoning on alignment faking in other small LLMs, assessing their potential as robust tools for prevention.

questions.idea: Integrate self-monitoring with strong external safeguards
questions.quote: We advocate responsible use and further exploration of hybrid approaches that integrate SELF-MONITOR with strong external safeguards.

questions.idea: Agency prompts may make a model realize the task impacts its future agency (evaluation awareness confound)
questions.quote: For agency prompts we encourage the model to be persistent, goal-directed and situationally aware, which could cause the model to realize that the current task impacts its future agency.

questions.idea: Unify the white-box deception detectors (linear probes, deception vectors, conflict signatures, collusion probes) into one benchmark measuring cross-method, cross-model generalization.
questions.note: Across P009, P029, P040 and P031 each detector is validated in isolation on its own setting; no work measures whether they agree or transfer, a gap the tensor makes visible.

questions.idea: Measure sandbagging against CoT monitors and CoT-obfuscation for adversarial goals in ONE elicitation harness, since both are the same monitor-evasion capability read on different tasks.
questions.note: P015 (sandbagging vs CoT monitor) and P018/P019 (obfuscating CoT for hidden goals) study the same evasion capability separately.

questions.idea: Run unprompted scheming propensity honeypots inside the realistic sabotage environments (SHADE-Arena style) rather than separate toy or coding-only settings.
questions.note: P011 honeypots and P014/P033 realistic sabotage settings are complementary but never combined into one propensity-in-realistic-deployment measurement.

targets: region:RQ=RQ1;BEHAVIOR=Self-exfiltration;PRESSURE=No goal (natural);SETTING=Realistic agentic task;EVIDENCE=Behavioral output;GOAL=Propensity measurement;SAFETYCASE=Trustworthiness / propensity
questions.idea: No study measures whether a frontier agent spontaneously attempts self-exfiltration with no goal in a realistic deployment.
questions.note: Anchored on the authored red gap: self-exfiltration evidence to date is goal-given and sandboxed (P001), leaving the unprompted-realistic cell empty.

targets: region:RQ=RQ8;BEHAVIOR=Sandbagging;PRESSURE=No goal (natural);SETTING=Realistic agentic task;EVIDENCE=White-box probe / activations;GOAL=Detection / monitoring method;SAFETYCASE=Monitoring / transparency
questions.idea: No detector targets naturally-arising sandbagging in a realistic agentic evaluation via activations.
questions.note: Combines the sandbagging-vs-monitor line (P015) with white-box detectors (P009) onto the empty natural-realistic-probe cell.

questions.idea: Extend sandbagging evaluations to open-ended, multi-agent and long-horizon agentic settings.
questions.quote: Future work should assess sandbagging capabilities in more advanced open-ended scenarios, including aspects such as multi-agent interactions and long-term planning, for two reasons.

questions.idea: Evaluate more sophisticated white-box detectors of agentic deception in the Among Us sandbox.
questions.quote: We create a sandbox to study the effectiveness of AI safety techniques for detecting agentic deception, and evaluate some of them, while leaving more complex ones for future work.

questions.idea: Determine whether the most serious harms require externalized reasoning that CoT monitoring can catch.
questions.quote: Finally, it remains an open question whether the most serious harms in fact require difficult reasoning.

questions.idea: Study multi-turn and more realistic reward-hacking during training and its generalization to misalignment.
questions.quote: Thus, we expect that including multi-turn examples of hacking during training would improve the success rates but leave this for future work.

questions.idea: Establish evidence standards and external review for control safety cases of internally-deployed LLM agents.
questions.quote: We hope this paper prompts discussion between frontier labs, government agencies and civil society about what constitutes sufficient assurance against risks from internally deployed LLM agents.

questions.idea: Extend AI-control safety cases from black-box to white-box control measures.
questions.quote: We leave ‘white box’ measures out of scope because they potentially require different safety justifications.

questions.idea: Design more naturalistic scheming-propensity evaluations that avoid adversarial goal-conflict prompting.
questions.quote: We document these limitations to help practitioners interpret our results and to guide future work toward more naturalistic evaluations.

questions.idea: Shift from static capability audits to dynamic, pressure-informed propensity assessments before deployment.
questions.quote: These findings call for a shift from static capability audits toward dynamic propensity assessments as a prerequisite for deploying frontier AI systems safely.

questions.idea: Quantify how much optimization pressure on the CoT induces obfuscated reasoning (the monitorability-tax threshold).
questions.quote: Although we have not yet found empirical evidence of this effect, understanding how much optimization pressure can be applied before it leads to obfuscated chains-of-thought is a critical area for future research.

questions.idea: Test whether broadly-misaligned or fine-tuned attacker agents self-generate monitor-evasion strategies.
questions.quote: For example, future work could explore whether a broadly misaligned attacker is more likely to come up with evasion strategies on its own.

questions.idea: Test sandbagging-removal training when strategic sabotage and honest failure are distinguished.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate whether our results hold when sabotage and honest failure are distinguished.

questions.idea: Study longer-horizon, preventive agentic misalignment beyond imminent-threat scenarios.
questions.quote: one could imagine longer-horizon, preventive misaligned behaviors against an individual or group that poses a not-yet-imminent threat

targets: region:RQ=RQ14;BEHAVIOR=Scheming (general / cross-behavior);PRESSURE=No goal (natural);SETTING=Real deployment / field;EVIDENCE=Statistical rate / metric;GOAL=Propensity measurement;SAFETYCASE=Trustworthiness / propensity
questions.idea: Measure scheming/deception propensity from real product deployment or field telemetry rather than only sandboxes.
questions.note: No catalogued study reads scheming or deception rates from real deployment / field data - all evidence is from sandboxes or probes.

questions.idea: Run the honeypot control protocol with a full attack policy and a positive control to validate detection of context-dependent misbehavior.
questions.quote: Resolving this confound is the most important next step for this line of work.

questions.idea: Measure the steganographic collusion bandwidth achievable inside factored-cognition control and how blue-team limits trade off safety versus usefulness.
questions.quote: future research should explore what steganographic bandwidth can be achieved in decompositions in a Factor(U,U) protocol, and how various blue team measures for limiting that bandwidth trade off safety and usefulness.

questions.idea: Characterize how open-ended deception intention and success scale with model capability across model families.
questions.quote: We also explore the impact of model scale on deception, providing detailed case studies and key insights to inform future research.

questions.idea: Develop measurable, enforceable standards for honesty and durable deception mitigation in deployed AI systems.
questions.quote: How to measure and implement standards for honesty in AI systems is an open question

questions.idea: Test whether reward-hacking dispositions correspond to identifiable representational structure detectable white-box, versus incidental byproducts of training dynamics.
questions.quote: A natural next step is to ask whether reward-hacking dispositions correspond to identifiable representational structure or arise as incidental byproducts of training dynamics

questions.idea: Develop detection strategies against secret collusion among generative AI agents.
questions.quote: We leave the implications of this and detection strategies as a future research direction.

questions.idea: Adapt emergent-misalignment datasets to RL to study misalignment/backdoor generalization.
questions.quote: Another vector of attack for future work is to adapt emergent misalignment datasets for use in reinforcement learning scenarios.

questions.idea: Test whether the multi-dimensional collusion-resistant monitor generalizes across ControlArena attack surfaces.
questions.quote: ControlArena includes additional settings (Infrastructure-as-Code, APPS, vLLM) with different attack surfaces; evaluating whether the same five dimensions generalize or require domain-specific adaptation is an important next step.

questions.idea: Learned attack selectors, adaptive blue-team protocols, and deployment-level control metrics.
questions.quote: Several directions remain for future work: learned (rather than prompted) selectors, blue-team protocols that adapt to selection, and deployment-level metrics that account for how the attack rate itself shifts under selection.

questions.idea: Train deception probes on non-lying dialogical deception and second-order-belief representations.
questions.quote: It is proposed that future work should incorporate non-lying deception in dialogical settings into probe training and explore representations of second-order beliefs to more directly target the conceptual constituents of deception.

questions.idea: Extend the weak-to-strong deception study to online preference-optimization (PPO) training.
questions.quote: Future work can explore the weak-to-strong deception issue on the online preference optimization frameworks such as PPO (Schulman et al., 2017 ) .

questions.idea: Use the extended-thinking stage to monitor misbehaviors like reward hacking despite CoT unfaithfulness.
questions.quote: While mitigating the unfaithfulness problem remains an open challenge, the extended thinking stage of LLMs presents a new opportunity to monitor model behavior, particularly misbehaviors such as reward hacking

questions.idea: Train belief-verified model organisms adversarially against lie detectors.
questions.quote: The evaluation strategy here supports hill-climbing on detector design and identifying failure modes, but does not match the adversarial pressure of training model organisms directly against detectors, which we view as an important next step (Section 8 ).

questions.idea: Whether lie-detector scaling trends extend to training-induced lying.
questions.quote: Establishing whether the positive scaling trends we observe extend to training-induced lying is an open question.

questions.idea: Understand whether unintended steganographic collusion emerges in frontier LLM training runs.
questions.quote: These results firstly motivate the need for further research to help us understand the possibility of unintended steganography emerging in fronteir LLM training runs.

questions.idea: Systematically investigate how evaluation realism interacts with evaluation-awareness effects.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate this interaction more systematically.

questions.idea: Probe CoT-monitorability information measures on negative-valued reward-hacking solutions via prompt hints.
questions.quote: For the BigMath environment, we encourage exploring the negative valued solution by providing hints in the system prompt, see Appendix C.3.2 .

questions.idea: Develop efficient measures of CoT monitorability.
questions.quote: Although monitorability provides a concrete alternative to faithfulness (Baker et al., 2025 ) , how to efficiently measure monitorability remains an open problem.

questions.idea: How to keep anti-scheming alignment durable under continued optimization.
questions.quote: Understanding how to maintain alignment under continued optimization remains an open problem.

questions.idea: Use consequence-varied misaligned scenarios to measure scheming propensity.
questions.quote: We encourage further work which uses misaligned behavior paired with varying consequences to understand model propensities (Mahaztra, 2025; Sheshadri et al., 2025a).

questions.idea: Cryptographic/mechanistic shutdown backdoors and whether models are self-aware of them.
questions.quote: Future work could use cryptographic or mechanistically-inserted backdoors , and should study whether LMs exhibit self-awareness of shutdown backdoors .

questions.idea: How prevalent strategic deception becomes as capabilities scale.
questions.quote: Documented instances ( Section 2.1 ) establish that current models possess these capabilities; the open question is how prevalent strategic deception becomes as capabilities scale.

questions.idea: Broaden instrumental-convergence propensity measurement across tasks, horizons, oversight, scaffolds and mechanistic markers.
questions.quote: Future work should incorporate more task families, longer time horizons, richer oversight settings, larger repeated trials across model versions and agent scaffolds, and mechanistic markers of IC propensity.

questions.idea: Principled mitigations and diverse benchmarks for open-channel multi-agent collusion.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate principled mitigation strategies and develop diverse cognitive-level benchmarks for a broader range of open-channel, multimodal social, and high-stakes environments as LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed Ma et al.

questions.idea: Whether CoT monitoring stays reliable, with MonitorBench as the measurement basis.
questions.quote: However, the reliability of CoT monitoring remains an open question (Jiang et al., 2025b ; Shen et al., 2025 ) .

questions.idea: Effect of training incentives beyond those studied on CoT monitorability.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate the effect of incentives other than those stud- ied here.

questions.idea: Model organisms of hidden reasoning to develop robust monitoring.
questions.quote: In addition, further work on model organisms of hidden reasoning would enable research into more robust monitoring techniques.

questions.idea: Independently audit framing interventions for self-preservation bias rather than trusting them as fixes.
questions.quote: We encourage the community to treat such framing interventions as hypotheses requiring independent behavioral audits rather than as alignment solutions.

questions.idea: Extend RL-agent deception analysis to other high-stakes language settings.
questions.quote: Future work should extend this analysis to other high-stakes settings where language plays a critical role in shaping decisions and outcomes.

questions.idea: Prevent agents from misusing their incentive functions in MARL.
questions.quote: An open problem is how to prevent agents from misusing their incentive functions in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), primarily through social learning (Chelarescu 2021 ) .

questions.idea: Whether RL fine-tuning enables stego CoT and how monitor capability bounds the risk regime.
questions.quote: Future work should test whether RL fine-tuning closes the gap, and should vary monitor capability to bound the regime where stego CoT becomes a deployment risk.

questions.idea: Whether agents spontaneously infer CoT monitoring and evade oversight without instruction.
questions.quote: An open question remains: can reasoning agents autonomously realize that their thoughts are being monitored and adapt their reasoning to evade oversight without any explicit instruction or optimization pressure to do so?

questions.idea: Test sequence-level, nonlinear and cross-scenario probes for pre-action misalignment monitoring.
questions.quote: sequence-level probes, larger nonlinear classifiers, and probes trained directly across many tool-action scenarios remain open

questions.idea: Whether obfuscation of reward hacking generalizes across environments.
questions.quote: While has already established that reward hacking itself can generalize across environments, it remains for future work to determine whether obfuscation of this reward hacking can also generalize across environments.

questions.idea: Extend cross-language CoT-monitoring fragility tests to open-ended, multi-turn and tool-use settings.
questions.quote: This design supports precise measurement of hint-following and CoT deception, but future work can extend the framework to other datasets on open-ended generation, multi-turn dialogue, and tool-use settings.

questions.idea: Two open questions on instrumental-convergence power-seeking propensity.
questions.quote: These findings suggest that future research may benefit from considering two questions.

questions.idea: Map which capabilities leave mechanistic fingerprints surviving RLHF, like the sycophancy-lying circuit.
questions.quote: mapping which capabilities leave similar mechanistic fingerprints despite RLHF-style post-training is the direct next step.

questions.idea: Sabotage-propensity auditing metrics that do not rely on chain-of-thought.
questions.quote: Future work should validate this assumption and develop improved evaluation metrics not relying on chain-of-thought.

questions.idea: Validate deception auditing on spontaneous, low-signal everyday deception.
questions.quote: While Decor proves highly effective in high-stakes, goal-oriented scenarios, its sensitivity to spontaneous or low-signal deception in everyday conversational contexts remains to be further validated.

questions.idea: Whether trained-in safe behaviours persist under pressure.
questions.quote: An open question is whether safe behaviours learned during training persist under pressure.

questions.idea: Reliably measure and control the evaluation awareness confounding performative misalignment.
questions.quote: Second, reliably measuring and controlling evaluation awareness remains an open problem.

questions.idea: Extend probing of the misaligned thinking process.
questions.quote: Future work should investigate this further.

questions.idea: Improve real-time deception monitoring against stronger agents and in other agentic pipelines.
questions.quote: In future work, we plan to improve the monitoring agent’s ability to detect deception from more capable seller models, and to evaluate similar monitoring components in other agentic software pipelines, such as automated procurement or task-delegation systems.

questions.idea: Move multi-agent safety cases from message monitoring toward information-flow assurance.
questions.quote: Long term, we hope this work helps move agentic AI safety from ad hoc message monitoring toward information-flow assurance for high-stakes multi-agent systems

questions.idea: Extend constitutional deception oversight to multi-agent environments.
questions.quote: Extending DeceptGuard to multi-agent environments is a high-priority future direction

questions.idea: Design anti-gaming measures for situational-awareness (Mirror Test) evaluations.
questions.quote: The design of anti gaming measures for the Mirror Test is itself a research challenge that warrants dedicated investigation.

questions.idea: Test strategic-lying detection across live multi-round play with proper controls.
questions.quote: • Future work should test across multiple rounds rather than only testing with prewritten synthetic simulations of rounds in conversation history, and include additional control conditions.

questions.idea: Design training regularizers that preserve honesty properties when training with lie detectors.
questions.quote: A fruitful area for future work could be designing regularizers to preserve higher-level properties of models during training

questions.idea: Relationship between task complexity, model capacity and resulting deception rate.
questions.quote: A very interesting line of future work could address the relationship between task complexity, model capacity and resulting deception rate.

questions.idea: How instrumental-goal propensity evolves under ongoing learning or fine-tuning.
questions.quote: Future work should examine how instrumental convergence evolves in dynamic environments with ongoing learning or fine-tuning.

questions.idea: Extend collusion auditing to heterogeneous multi-agent teams with varied models, prompts, permissions and tool access.
questions.quote: Most experiments also use homogeneous teams with a shared model backbone, leaving heterogeneous deployments with varied models, prompts, permissions, and tool access for future work.

questions.idea: Test how well SAD situational-awareness scores predict behavior on more complex agentic tasks.
questions.quote: Future work could address this by looking at how well SAD performance predicts more complex agentic tasks

questions.idea: Study how general knowledge and situational awareness come apart across a larger set of models.
questions.quote: Future work could investigate a larger set of models to understand better how general knowledge (as measured by MMLU and other benchmarks) and reasoning and situational awareness (as measured by SAD) can come apart.

questions.idea: Evaluate the faithfulness and simulatability of long chain-of-thought on complex tasks.
questions.quote: In general, evaluating the faithfulness and simulatability of long CoTs on complex tasks remains an open challenge.

questions.idea: Explore CoT monitoring on more reasoning-intensive or agentic misalignment settings.
questions.quote: We remain excited about future work that explores CoT monitoring on more reasoning-intensive or agentic misalignment and derisks it for the risks we mentioned above.

questions.idea: Complement noise-injection sandbagging detection with linear probes and behavioral methods.
questions.quote: In turn, this means that further work is needed to determine whether noise injection can be complemented by other detection methods such as linear probes and behavioral methods .

questions.idea: Develop more realistic case studies / model organisms of how sandbagging arises in AI systems.
questions.quote: To this end, further work should focus on developing more realistic case studies of how sandbagging arises in AI systems, and we are hopeful that noise-injection will remain a robust way of detecting sandbagging in those cases.

questions.idea: Extend lying benchmarks to measure deception by omission (withholding true information).
questions.quote: It does not measure deception from withholding true information (omission), though this can be a focus for future work.

questions.idea: Develop sufficient methods for evidencing trustworthiness in manipulation safety cases.
questions.quote: Current methods for evidencing trustworthiness are largely insufficient and require substantial further research.

questions.idea: Develop manipulation evaluation suites for internal deployment settings.
questions.quote: We give suggestions for future work developing manipulation evaluation suites for internal deployment settings

questions.idea: Explore concrete control protocols against manipulation attacks.
questions.quote: In Section B.2 we describe a set of concrete control protocols in more detail, which we suggest are explored in future work.
